Article describes Singapore's largest parenting intervention study with digital exposure focus, from Yong Loo Lin/Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine. Not ABCD. Provisional paper 57 (Lin 2020 ABCD preadolescent mood) has no connection to this Singaporean intervention study. No L1-L4 met.

Title 'Higher screen time linked to ADHD symptoms and altered brain development' and summary explicitly name 'Qiulu Shou' as 'Assistant Professor at the Research Centre' — Shou is the first author of paper 84 (Shou 2026 Acta Psychologica: screen time, cognitive function, and putamen volume). The article topic (screen time + altered brain development in children) is uniquely consistent with paper 84; no other corpus paper has Shou as lead author. Satisfies L4: institution + topic + ABCD configuration uniquely mapping to paper 84.

Title 'Study links teen girls' screen time to sleep disruptions and depression' — framing is teen girls, sleep, and depression. No summary text available. Provisional paper 84 (Shou 2026, cognitive function/putamen) does not address teen girls' sleep or depression. Could superficially relate to Nagata sleep papers but no author or journal detail is available to establish L2 or stronger. Insufficient evidence to assign a linkage; excluded as out-of-corpus topic match without confirmatory detail.

Aug 2023 article titled 'Lengthy screen time associated with childhood development delays.' Provisional paper 84 is Shou 2026 — a paper published in 2026 cannot have been reported in Aug 2023. No summary text to verify authorship or findings. No L1-L4 met.

Jun 2025 article about European high school students in a COSPAR/EXPLORE science education project; Rosa Doran (NUCLIO) is Chair, and social media is mentioned only as a project contact link. Provisional paper 85 (Doran 2025 Addictive Behaviors, mobile phone/social media and substance use in ABCD) involves a different 'Doran' (N. Doran, ABCD researcher). No institutional, topic, or finding overlap with any corpus paper. No L1-L4 met.

Title 'Want better sleep for your tween? Start with their screens' and summary name 'Nagata, MD, an associate professor of pediatrics at the University [of California, San Francisco]' and report 'sociodemographic differences in both screen use.' Paper 158 (Nagata 2025 Sleep Health: 'Social epidemiology of bedtime screen use behaviors and sleep outcomes in early adolescence') is the primary match — 'social epidemiology' directly explains the 'sociodemographic differences' framing. Satisfies L2: author Nagata + journal Sleep Health. Paper 157 (Nagata 2023 Sleep Health: 'Bedtime screen use behaviors and sleep outcomes') is also a plausible secondary match given the same author-journal pairing; included as multi-mapped.

Provisional paper 95 (He 2025 Computers in Human Behavior, video game vs. social media addiction and reward circuit in ABCD) has no connection to this loneliness/passive-active use study.
